label: Valley
_model: Wild kernel that keeps you by being kind. The appetite belongs to the valley — it wants nothing to go over the top, everything to come in out of the wind, everything to end up at the bottom, and its own sky. Every cruelty here looks like hospitality, which is what makes it hard to leave.

appetites.want: that nothing should ever go over the top
appetites.purpose: everything would stay in the bottom

appeasement.move: go up to the ridge and come back down without crossing

appetites.want: that everything should come in out of the wind
appetites.purpose: nothing would ever be cold outside it

appeasement.move: come in and sit down at a fire that is not yours

appetites.want: that everything should come down to it and stay
appetites.purpose: nothing would ever be taken back up
appetites.asks: "You're not taking that up with you?"

appeasement.move: put something down at the bottom and leave it there

appetites.want: never to share a sky with anywhere else
appetites.purpose: the weather would always be its own
appetites.conscript: the ones who wanted a view

appeasement.move: wait out one turn of its weather without complaining

hearth.label: the fire that was kept in for whoever came
hearth.function: the only warmth here that was never a trap

return.label: the thing that came down and was carried back up
return.function: the only thing that ever left the bottom again

sky.label: the one clear day, kept
sky.function: the only time anybody here saw out

factions.name: the Kept In
factions.essence: came in out of the weather and have been very comfortable ever since

factions.name: the drove
factions.essence: were taking stock through and the top closed on them

factions.name: the cloud that sits in it
factions.essence: is not weather and does not lift

factions.name: what comes down the beck
factions.essence: has only ever gone one way, which is down

triggerGlossary.announced: came in at the valley mouth in daylight and were seen from the farms
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: seen on the tops twice from the bottom
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice in a bottom where every sound comes back off both sides
triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed one night, which is how it starts
triggerGlossary.disturbed: took a wall down, went over the col, or carried something up out of the bottom

skirmish.line: 2 Dire Wolves in the hanging wood

foes.name: Dire Wolf
foes.note: work you back down toward the bottom

skirmish.avoid: they will not follow you up onto the open ridge

fight.line: 4 Bandits who came in and could not get out again

foes.name: Bandit
foes.note: desperate rather than wicked; they want food and a way over

fight.avoid: tell them where the col is and they will take it and go

battle.line: 1 Troll at the head wall and 2 Dire Wolves

foes.name: Troll
foes.note: REGENERATES 2 Grit a round unless the wound was burnt

battle.harmedBy: anything, but the Troll only stays down if fire touches it — say so before initiative; there is wood in the hanging wood
battle.avoid: it holds the head wall and nothing else; the col is a longer climb and it is clear

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith on the col, 1 Troll, 1 Ogre and 2 Dire Wolves

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit; it stands in the one way out

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest, fire for the Troll
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

ridges.dangerLine: the valley has one way over and it would rather you did not know which

institution: ridges on both sides running unbroken for miles
one notch in the skyline and cloud sitting in it
walls running up both sides to the very top, as though to finish the job
ritual: the tops walked once a year by somebody and nobody else ever
a cairn kept on the col by whoever goes over
a gate in the top wall left shut, always
demand: a skyline with one notch in it that you can only see from one field
a gate in the top wall standing shut with the ground worn on both sides
a track going up and stopping at the wall
wound: a col with the cairn thrown down into the valley
top walls built up higher than any stock needs
a track up to the ridge grassed over in one season
anchor: the one notch in the skyline that goes over
a cairn on the col that stands
a gate in the top wall that opens

features: a notch in the skyline seen from one field
a gate shut in a top wall
a track stopping at a wall
a cairn thrown down off a col
top walls built higher than needed
a path grassed over in one season

decisions.cue: a skyline with one notch in it that you can only see from one field
decisions.cost: the notch is the way over and the field is the only place it shows

resolve.success: you fix the col from the field and can find it again from anywhere in the bottom
resolve.failure: you set off for it from the wrong side and the ridge closes up as you climb
resolve.orElse: stay in the bottom; there is no way over and the valley is very pleased

decisions.cue: a gate in the top wall standing shut with the ground worn on both sides
decisions.cost: things have gone through it both ways and it is shut now

resolve.success: you open it and the way over stays open behind you for everybody
resolve.failure: you climb the wall instead and knock the top off, and the valley notices: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it shut; the drove cannot get out either, and they were counting on you

decisions.cue: a track going up the fell and stopping dead at a wall
decisions.cost: the track was used and the wall is newer than the track

resolve.success: you find where the track resumed on the far side and the whole route is yours
resolve.failure: you go over the wall on a guess and are on the tops in the cloud
resolve.orElse: follow the wall along, costing a Turn and putting you at the head wall

decisions.cue: a cairn thrown down off the col into the valley
decisions.cost: somebody unmarked the way over deliberately

resolve.success: you rebuild it and the col is findable from the bottom by anyone, for good
resolve.failure: you leave it and can find the col once, by luck, and not again
resolve.orElse: carry the stones down instead; nothing will ever cross here again

decisions.cue: top walls built up higher than any stock ever needed
decisions.cost: the walls are not for sheep

resolve.success: you see what they are for and can get through or over at the one weak place
resolve.failure: you climb them where they are strongest and are seen doing it from the bottom
resolve.orElse: stay below the walls; the whole top of the valley is closed to you

decisions.cue: a path up to the ridge grassed over in a single season
decisions.cost: grass does not do that in a season without help

resolve.success: you find the line under the grass and can walk it up in the dark if you have to
resolve.failure: you take the obvious line instead, which is not the path, and it ends in crag
resolve.orElse: leave it; every route up from here is unmade ground

situations.doing: standing in a field looking up at a notch in the skyline
situations.onArrival: it points at the notch and then does not move
situations.because: it can see the way over and has never once gone toward it
situations.offer: go up to the col with it and it will show you the true line

situations.doing: standing shut in a wall on the very top of the ridge
situations.onArrival: the ground is worn deep on both sides of it and the latch is bright
situations.because: things went through both ways until somebody shut it
situations.offer: open it and the way over stays open behind you

situations.doing: standing at a head wall with stock that cannot climb
situations.onArrival: they ask whether the col is passable
situations.because: the top closed while they were coming through
situations.offer: tell them the way and they will drive you out with them

situations.doing: lying thrown down in the scree below a col
situations.onArrival: the stones are stacked at the bottom rather than scattered
situations.because: somebody unmarked the crossing on purpose
situations.offer: rebuild it and everything in the bottom can find the way out

situations.doing: standing unbroken in both directions with cloud lying along them
situations.onArrival: the cloud thins over exactly one point and closes again
situations.because: there is one way over and the valley hides it
situations.offer: watch for the thinning and it will show you the col, once

situations.doing: filling the whole head of the valley with walls that go up to the sky
situations.onArrival: the walls are higher at the top than at the bottom
situations.because: it wants nothing to go over and it has been building
situations.offer: tell it you are coming back and it will let you go up

temptations.cue: a knowledge of the one notch
temptations.benefit: once, find the way out from anywhere
temptations.standingDrawback: the valley closes the col to everyone else while you know it

temptations.cue: the pin out of the top gate
temptations.benefit: once, open a way that was shut
temptations.standingDrawback: it cannot be shut again behind you

temptations.cue: a stone off the col cairn
temptations.benefit: once, mark a crossing so it stays marked
temptations.standingDrawback: everything in the bottom follows the mark

temptations.cue: a line of the grassed-over path
temptations.benefit: walk up in the dark or the cloud
temptations.standingDrawback: the thing that grassed it over notices it being used

temptations.cue: a through-stone out of the top wall
temptations.benefit: once, get through what was built to hold you
temptations.standingDrawback: the wall is one stone weaker for everything else too

shelter.dangerLine: everything here wants you to come in and sit down, and it means it kindly

institution: a valley that is the only warm place for a day's walk in any direction
farms set so that no traveller ever has to pass a door
a chapel with the porch swept and the bench worn
ritual: a fire kept in overnight for anybody who comes
a bed made up in every house that is not being used
a traveller fed before being asked a single question
demand: a fire kept in with the chairs drawn round it and nobody in them
a bed made up and turned down in an empty house
a table laid for one more than there are
wound: fires kept in for years in houses with nobody left
a porch bench worn through by people waiting to be let out
beds made up in every room of a house with the door nailed
anchor: the fire that was kept in for whoever came
a house where the door opens outward as well
a bed that was slept in one night only

features: a fire kept in with chairs drawn round
a bed made up in an empty house
a table laid for one more
a porch bench worn through
a door that only opens inward
food set out and still warm

decisions.cue: a fire kept in with the chairs drawn round it and nobody sitting in them
decisions.cost: sitting down is the whole of it

resolve.success: you sit, and get up again before you are settled, and the valley respects that
resolve.failure: you sit and are comfortable, and the next area is a night later than you thought
resolve.orElse: stay standing in the doorway; you are cold and nothing here will speak to you

decisions.cue: a bed made up and turned down in a house with nobody in it
decisions.cost: one night is one night, they always say

resolve.success: you sleep on the floor instead and wake rested and still your own
resolve.failure: you sleep in the bed and the house counts you as staying: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: sleep out; the weather is the valley's and it knows where you are

decisions.cue: a table laid for one more than there are people in the house
decisions.cost: the extra place has been laid every night for years

resolve.success: you find who it is laid for and can carry that name to the ending
resolve.failure: you sit in the place and everything at the table welcomes you by their name
resolve.orElse: eat nothing; the household is offended and closes to you

decisions.cue: a porch bench worn through by people sitting on it a long time
decisions.cost: they were waiting to be let out, not in

resolve.success: you understand what the porch is really for and can leave any house at will
resolve.failure: you sit on the bench to rest and find the door behind you has closed
resolve.orElse: stand in the yard; you learn nothing and get wet doing it

decisions.cue: a door that opens inward and has no latch on the inside
decisions.cost: the house is not locked, exactly

resolve.success: you fit a latch on the inside and the house cannot keep anybody again
resolve.failure: you go in to look and the door is a door again, from the other side
resolve.orElse: stay out of the house; what is in it is what you needed

decisions.cue: food set out on a table and still warm in a cold house
decisions.cost: somebody cooked it and there is nobody to have cooked it

resolve.success: you thank the house aloud and eat, and it feeds you honestly for the delve
resolve.failure: you eat without thanking and are a guest now, in the full sense: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: go hungry; -1 die on Brawn until you eat somewhere else, and there is nowhere else

situations.doing: burning in a grate with four chairs drawn round it and nobody in them
situations.onArrival: the chairs are warm and the fire has just been made up
situations.because: the fire is kept in for whoever comes and nobody has come
situations.offer: sit down for exactly as long as it takes to get warm, and the house will help you

situations.doing: laying a table for one more than there are
situations.onArrival: it sets the extra place and looks up at you
situations.because: the place is laid every night for somebody who went over the top
situations.offer: take the place and it will tell you who left and how

situations.doing: making up a bed in a room nobody uses
situations.onArrival: she asks how many of you there are, and how long
situations.because: she has been making beds since before the top closed
situations.offer: tell her one night and she will tell you the way over

situations.doing: standing swept with a bench worn through in the middle
situations.onArrival: the bench is warm and the chapel door behind it is shut
situations.because: people sat here a long time waiting to be let out
situations.offer: sit and get up again, and the valley will let you go

situations.doing: standing in a doorway with a lamp, holding the door open
situations.onArrival: the wind at your back drops the moment it opens the door
situations.because: it is the only warm place and it knows it
situations.offer: accept one hour of it and it will give you the run of the valley

situations.doing: standing laid and steaming in a house with the fire out
situations.onArrival: the food is hot and the room is cold enough to see your breath
situations.because: the house feeds whoever comes and nobody comes
situations.offer: thank the house aloud before you eat and it will not keep you

temptations.cue: an ember off the fire kept in
temptations.benefit: be welcome anywhere in the valley
temptations.standingDrawback: welcome here is very hard to leave

temptations.cue: an inside latch off a door
temptations.benefit: once, keep a place from keeping you
temptations.standingDrawback: the door you took it from cannot be shut at all now

temptations.cue: the extra place at the table
temptations.benefit: once, be expected and provided for
temptations.standingDrawback: you are expected every night from now on

temptations.cue: a night's rest in a made bed
temptations.benefit: recover as though you had slept properly
temptations.standingDrawback: the house counts you as staying

temptations.cue: a knowledge of the porch bench
temptations.benefit: once, leave a place that wants you to stay
temptations.standingDrawback: somebody else waits on the bench in your place

bottom.dangerLine: everything in this valley ends up at the bottom eventually, including you

institution: a bottom made entirely of what used to be on the sides
a beck that only ever runs one way and takes everything with it
fields at the bottom that have never once needed manuring
ritual: what comes down laid out at the bottom and left
nothing carried back up, by custom, by anybody
the beck walked down each spring and what is in it collected
demand: a heap of what has come down with the newest things on top
a beck with something in it that has stopped moving
a field at the bottom with a shape under the turf
wound: a bottom dug over by somebody looking for one thing
the beck dammed so that nothing more comes down
a heap gone through and everything of value taken up
anchor: the thing that came down and was carried back up
a record of everything the bottom has

features: a heap with the newest things on top
something stopped in the beck
a shape under the turf of a field
a bottom dug over recently
a dam across a beck
things laid out and left

decisions.cue: a heap of what has come down with the newest things on top
decisions.cost: the newest things are recent and one of them is not a thing

resolve.success: you go through the top of the heap and find what came down last, and when
resolve.failure: you dig into the heap and the whole side of it comes down on you
resolve.orElse: leave the heap; you never learn what has recently arrived at the bottom

decisions.cue: a beck with something in it that has stopped moving
decisions.cost: the beck takes everything down and this has stuck

resolve.success: you free it and the beck runs clear, and what was behind it comes down usefully
resolve.failure: you free it and everything held behind it comes down at once, onto you
resolve.orElse: leave it stuck; the beck backs up and the bottom ground floods

decisions.cue: a field at the bottom with a shape under the turf
decisions.cost: the field has never needed manuring and this is why

resolve.success: you identify what is under it without opening the ground, and it names the transgression
resolve.failure: you open the ground and the field is no longer a field, and the valley minds
resolve.orElse: leave the turf; the ending has no body and no proof

decisions.cue: a bottom dug over recently by somebody looking for one particular thing
decisions.cost: they were looking and they may have found it

resolve.success: you work out what they were after and whether they got it, and both matter
resolve.failure: you dig where they dug and find what they were careful to leave
resolve.orElse: leave the diggings; somebody else has the thing and you do not know who

decisions.cue: a dam thrown across the beck so that nothing more comes down
decisions.cost: damming the beck is the only defiance anybody here has managed

resolve.success: you keep the dam and the bottom stops taking; the valley is furious and constrained
resolve.failure: you break it and everything held up behind it goes to the bottom at once
resolve.orElse: leave it; it fails on its own within the Turn, which is worse

decisions.cue: things laid out at the bottom in rows and left, none of them taken
decisions.cost: carrying anything up is the one thing nobody here does

resolve.success: you carry one thing up and the valley's hold breaks a little, permanently
resolve.failure: you carry it up and something comes up after it, and it is not pleased
resolve.orElse: leave the rows; nothing has ever left the bottom and nothing will

situations.doing: lying at the bottom with everything the valley has taken, newest on top
situations.onArrival: something on the top of it is still warm
situations.because: everything comes down and nothing goes up
situations.offer: take one thing off the top and carry it up, and the valley loosens

situations.doing: laying things out at the bottom in rows, carefully
situations.onArrival: it sets one down and looks up to see whether you approve
situations.because: what comes down is laid out and left
situations.offer: carry one row's worth up and it will tell you everything the bottom holds

situations.doing: turning over the bottom ground with a spade and no hurry
situations.onArrival: he asks whether you know what a thing looks like
situations.because: he has been looking for one particular thing for years
situations.offer: tell him and he will give you everything else he has turned up

situations.doing: running down with something stuck in it that has stopped the water
situations.onArrival: the water above the block is rising and the water below is clear
situations.because: it takes everything down and this will not go
situations.offer: free it and the beck will carry you down anywhere, fast

situations.doing: lying green at the bottom with a shape showing under the turf
situations.onArrival: the grass over the shape is greener than the rest
situations.because: the field has never needed manuring
situations.offer: name what is under it and the valley will admit what it did

situations.doing: filling the whole floor of the valley with what used to be on the sides
situations.onArrival: the ground gives very slightly wherever you put your foot
situations.because: everything comes down to it and stays
situations.offer: leave it something willingly and it will let you take something up

temptations.cue: the thing that was carried back up
temptations.benefit: once, take something out of the bottom
temptations.standingDrawback: the valley takes something of yours down to replace it

temptations.cue: the digger's spade
temptations.benefit: once, find what the bottom has
temptations.standingDrawback: the ground opens for you wherever you carry it

temptations.cue: a record of what the bottom holds
temptations.benefit: know everything this valley has taken
temptations.standingDrawback: you know which of it was people

temptations.cue: a knowledge of how the dam was built
temptations.benefit: once, stop things coming down
temptations.standingDrawback: they come all at once when it goes

temptations.cue: something off the laid-out rows
temptations.benefit: once, have exactly what somebody lost
temptations.standingDrawback: they are at the bottom, and they want it

weather.dangerLine: the valley makes its own weather and it has not shared a sky with anywhere else in years

institution: cloud lying in the valley when the tops are clear
a bottom that gets the sun for two hours and the sides that get it all day
weather that comes in at the mouth and does not go out at the head
ritual: the sky looked at each morning and nothing said about it
washing hung out on the one good day and never since
a clear day marked on a doorframe with the date
demand: cloud lying at exactly head height and not lifting
a doorframe with one date cut into it and nothing after
washing on a line in weather that will not dry it
wound: a doorframe with the dates going up and then stopping
cloud that has been down so long the walls are green with it
a sundial in a garden that has not been used in living memory
anchor: a doorframe with every clear day cut on it
a sky you can see out of

features: cloud lying at head height
a doorframe with one date cut in it
washing that will not dry
walls green with standing cloud
a sundial gone unused
two hours of sun in a bottom

decisions.cue: cloud lying at exactly head height and showing no sign of lifting
decisions.cost: you can go up through it or wait it out

resolve.success: you wait it out without complaining and it lifts for you, properly, once
resolve.failure: you push up through it and are on the tops in cloud, without a line
resolve.orElse: go along the bottom instead; it costs a Turn and the cloud comes down further

decisions.cue: a doorframe with clear days cut into it and the dates stopping
decisions.cost: the last date is the last time anybody saw out

resolve.success: you read the dates and know exactly when the valley closed its sky
resolve.failure: you cut today's date in and the valley takes that as a claim about the weather
resolve.orElse: leave the frame; you have no idea how long this has been going on

decisions.cue: washing on a line in weather that has never been going to dry it
decisions.cost: somebody hung it out hoping, and hopes still

resolve.success: you take it in for them and the household will do anything you ask
resolve.failure: you leave it and the household takes that as a judgement on them
resolve.orElse: take it in and keep it; you have dry cloth and an enemy in the house

decisions.cue: walls green with cloud that has been lying against them for years
decisions.cost: the green is the measure of it

resolve.success: you read the growth and know this is older than anybody living here
resolve.failure: you scrape it off to see the stone and the cloud comes down to the ground
resolve.orElse: ignore the walls; you take the valley's word for how long this has been

decisions.cue: a sundial in a garden that nobody living has ever seen work
decisions.cost: it was set up when there was sun to set it by

resolve.success: you set it right and the valley remembers it had a sky, and thins, once
resolve.failure: you take the gnomon and the garden loses its last claim on daylight
resolve.orElse: leave it; there is no reckoning of time here at all and the Turns blur

decisions.cue: two hours of sun reaching the bottom and the sides lit all day
decisions.cost: the light is up there and you are down here

resolve.success: you time the two hours and can be exactly where you need the light to be
resolve.failure: you plan by the light on the sides and are in the dark at the bottom
resolve.orElse: move by feel; every roll in the next area is at -1 die for the dark

situations.doing: lying in the valley at head height with the tops clear above it
situations.onArrival: it thins around you and closes again behind
situations.because: the valley makes its own weather and will not lift for anybody
situations.offer: wait in it without complaining and it will lift and show you out

situations.doing: cutting a date into a doorframe with a knife
situations.onArrival: it stops and asks whether today counts as clear
situations.because: clear days are cut in and there has not been one
situations.offer: tell it today counts and the cloud lifts as far as the ridge

situations.doing: hanging washing in weather that will never dry it
situations.onArrival: she asks whether you think it will clear
situations.because: she has hung it out every day since it closed
situations.offer: take it in for her and she will tell you the two hours the sun reaches

situations.doing: standing in a garden with the gnomon bright and the dial green
situations.onArrival: a patch of sun crosses it while you stand there and then goes
situations.because: it was set when there was sun and nobody has seen it work
situations.offer: set it true and the valley will give you its one clear day

situations.doing: sitting in the head of the valley with the cloud coming off it
situations.onArrival: the cloud pours downhill from it and does not disperse
situations.because: it will not share a sky with anywhere else
situations.offer: bear its weather once, without complaint, and it will show you the top

situations.doing: reaching the bottom of the valley for exactly two hours
situations.onArrival: the light comes and goes at the same points on the wall
situations.because: the sides get it all day and the bottom gets almost none
situations.offer: be where the light falls and everything here will deal with you honestly

temptations.cue: the one clear day, kept
temptations.benefit: once, have the weather you need
temptations.standingDrawback: the valley takes it back double, and chooses when

temptations.cue: a piece of the dated doorframe
temptations.benefit: know when this place closed its sky
temptations.standingDrawback: the valley knows you have counted

temptations.cue: the gnomon off the sundial
temptations.benefit: once, know exactly what hour it is
temptations.standingDrawback: the garden it came from has no time at all

temptations.cue: dry cloth from a line that never dried
temptations.benefit: once, be warm and dry in its weather
temptations.standingDrawback: a household here is offended and stays that way

temptations.cue: a knowledge of the two hours
temptations.benefit: be in the light when you need to be
temptations.standingDrawback: so is everything that has been waiting for it
